items.text: Oil prices surged 10% WoW (WTI +$9.76 to $107.02; Brent +$21.29 to $130.80), driven by Middle East conflict disruptions of energy supplies. Energy shock remains primarily price-driven rather than wage-driven, but ECB warned on geopolitical upside risks to inflation and potential winter supply disruptions. This replicates 2022-23 shock dynamics, with special-situations investors exposed to energy hedges, high-yield energy refinancings, and credit quality compression in energy-dependent corporates.

Fed hiked 25bp to 4.0% on 2026-09-17 amid tightening labor market signals but decelerating wage growth (AHE 3.09% YoY, down from 3.24%). Jobless claims remain benign at 196K. Unemployment flat at 4.1% with August payrolls at +162K (though July looks revised lower at 21K). Slower wage growth and solid jobless metrics support the case for continued tightening despite inflation concerns. Special-situations credit investors should monitor whether labor softening accelerates—a key recession trigger.

Core inflation remains sticky (core PCE 2.45% YoY, core CPI still well-behaved); headline inflation elevated by energy (headline CPI 3.35%, headline PCE 3.7%). PPI surprised sharply up to 5.41% YoY (from 4.8%), signaling pipeline pressures. Consumer sentiment collapsed again (preliminary September at 47.8 vs. expected 51.0) with one-year inflation expectations at 4.6%—highest in months. Inflation de-anchoring risk is rising and pushing Fed tightening; credit duration risk remains acute.

ECB raised deposit rate to 2.50% on 10 September 2026, second hike since Iran conflict began. Interest-rate futures are pricing in a third ECB hike by December. Fed hiked 25bp to 4.0% today; market is now ~82% confident on another September 18-19 hike. Yield curve inverted further (10-2 compression to 27bp from 33bp)—classic late-cycle signal. Central banks synchronized tight, restricting credit cycle outlook.

HY OAS widened 5bp to 270bp; IG OAS flat at 78bp; CCC OAS anchored at 1076bp. Spreads compressed but showing early cracks as energy and input cost shocks filter into credit. Volatility (VIX) rose to 17.71 from 16.46—a low level, suggesting complacency. Special-situations investors should note: 2-10 inversion + rising PPI + collapsing sentiment = classic setup for credit dislocations in leveraged/energy-exposed sectors.

GDPNow tracking 5.08% (much higher than 1.5% actual Q2 print), likely reflecting recent data strength, though Q2's 1.5% (down from 2.1% Q1) showed underlying weakness. Manufacturing PMI remains expansionary (Aug 54.6, down 1pt but still healthy) with 8 straight months of growth; ISM Services at 55.4 (Aug, +1.3bp). Demand is moderating (new orders down 3pt to 53.7), signaling late-cycle deceleration. Growth narrative is bifurcated: backward data strong, forward orders softening—classic pre-slowdown pattern.

Consumer sentiment collapsed to 47.8 (Sept prelim, well below 51.0 expected), lowest since mid-May, driven by gasoline prices and inflation fears. Mortgage rates jumped to 6.95% from 6.76% (20bp WoW); housing starts fell to 1.275M (Aug), down 26K; existing home sales at 3.98M (Aug), down 80K. Retail sales YoY at 6.93% (strong, but July saw 5.76%), but that was before sentiment cratered. Housing and household formation at acute risk if sentiment continues lower and rate pressures persist.

themeCards.title: Energy-driven inflation shock widens
themeCards.statusLine: WTI +$9.76 to $107 in 2 days; Brent +$21.29 to $130.80. Middle East conflict continues to disrupt supply. ECB warned of further winter supply risk if storage low + cold weather.
themeCards.relevance: Corporates with high energy content (chemicals, logistics, manufacturing) facing margin compression. Energy-linked refinancings will tighten; high-yield energy credits under pressure. Commodity-hedged credit opportunities in weakness.

themeCards.title: Fed tightening cycle extends; recession risk rising
themeCards.statusLine: Fed hiked 25bp to 4.0% Sept 17; market pricing ~82% odds of another hike Sept 18-19. 2-10 curve inverted (27bp) with no cuts priced near-term. Wage growth cooling (AHE 3.09%) but core inflation still 2.45% and PPI at 5.41%.
themeCards.relevance: Extended tight policy window squeezes weak credits and refinancing walls. Watch for: leverage covenant stress, working capital pressures on low-margin corporates, and higher rollover risk. CCC and B-rated floaters may face acute re-pricing if real rates stay elevated.

themeCards.title: Consumer sentiment collapses; housing demand at risk
themeCards.statusLine: UMich Sept preliminary 47.8 (vs 51.0 exp, down -6% MoM from Aug 51.7). Worst reading since May 2026 peak panic. One-year inflation expectations at 4.6%—highest in months. Mortgage rates at 6.95%.
themeCards.relevance: Demand destruction signal for housing, consumer durables, and discretionary retail. Resi mortgage servicers and originators face volume cliffs. Homebuilder credits tighten further. Consumer cyclical credits (autos, furniture, retail) face demand cliff risk if sentiment stays depressed.

themeCards.title: Manufacturing demand losing steam; orders roll over
themeCards.statusLine: ISM Mfg Aug 54.6 (down 1pt from July 55.6); new orders collapsed 3pt to 53.7 (down from 56.7). Production still robust (58.3) but backlogs fell 3.2pt to 51.8. Employment eased to 51.2. Prices index sticky at 71.1.
themeCards.relevance: Early warning of capex / industrial demand slowdown. Equipment lessors, industrial services, and B2B manufacturers vulnerable to order book deterioration. Leverage multiples at risk if revenue growth inflects; watch for covenant pressure in industrial credit pools.

themeCards.title: Geopolitical supply-chain disruption (Iran/Middle East)
themeCards.statusLine: Supertanker fires reported in Strait of Hormuz; oil price volatility remains elevated. ECB explicitly cited Middle East conflict and Russia war as upside inflation risks. Insurance and logistics costs spiking.
themeCards.relevance: Direct hit to credit quality in shipping, insurance, and energy-intensive exports. Refinancing costs for disruption-exposed credit rise. Hedging costs spike, eroding margins. Watch for supply-chain financing stress in low-liquidity corporates and smaller exporters.

themeCards.title: China growth faltering amid slowing global demand
themeCards.statusLine: NBS official PMI Aug 49.8 (contraction, though best in months); Caixin Aug 50.9 (marginal expansion, but well below typical). Domestic demand soft despite policy support expectations. Export orders likely deteriorating.
themeCards.relevance: Spillover impact on US/EU commodity importers, exporters to China, and supply-chain exposures. Credit spreads for China-linked industrials under pressure. EM currency stress and carry-trade unwind potential if China fiscal stimulus disappoints. Refinancing risk for China-exposed credit.

ecb.delta: Sept 10 hike from 2.25%; second increase in 2026; more hikes priced for Dec

chinaPMI.delta: Official NBS Aug 49.8 (slightly above 49.6 exp); private Caixin Aug 50.9 (soft); both sub-50 but stabilizing

ismServices.delta: Aug 55.4 (up 1.3 from July 54.1); 26 consecutive months expansion; strong back-to-school and holiday prep activity

retailSales.delta: Aug +6.93% YoY (up from July +5.76%); strong print but pre-sentiment crash; m/m not available in search

existingHome.delta: Aug 3.98M SAAR (down 80K from July 4.06M); mild sequential softening amid higher mortgage rates

consensus.CPI: Expected ~3.2% YoY (headline); core ~2.5% YoY — next release mid-October
consensus.PCE: Expected headline ~3.6% YoY; core ~3.2% YoY — next release late October
consensus.PPI: Expected ~4.8% YoY final demand; next release early October
consensus.Retail Sales: Expected +0.3% to +0.5% m/m (ex-autos); next release early October
consensus.GDP: GDPNow tracking 5.08%; official Q3 2026 advance estimate due end of October

regime.label: Late-cycle tightening
regime.detail: Inverted curve, energy shock, cooling orders, collapsing sentiment, Fed hiking into slowdown — classic pre-recession credit cycle compression.
